review_candidates.title: Operations Manager, Global Strategic Accounts
review_candidates.description: About the Role The Operations Manager, Global Strategic Accounts oversees the day-to-day delivery of a large global enterprise account. This full-time role manages a distributed team of Wellbeing Coordinators and directs the work of contract Health Coaches assigned to the account. Working remotely in the United States, the Operations Manager enables coordinators and coaches to execute campaigns, live sessions, and other program activities across global regions. This role establishes clear expectations, resolves operational issues, and maintains consistent quality while accommodating local needs. The Operations Manager partners closely with the Program Manager on delivery plans and capacity, the Account Director on account priorities and escalations, and the Director of Coaching Operations on coaching standards and quality. While the Program Manager owns program scope and delivery timelines, the Operations Manager owns delivery execution, staffing assignments, and team capacity. Key Responsibilities Lead the global delivery team by hiring, onboarding, managing, and developing Wellbeing Coordinators, establishing clear expectations, providing regular feedback, and addressing performance concerns. Direct contract coaches day-to-day by setting program goals, defining success metrics, providing clear guidance on live events, and aligning coach activities with account strategy. Assign and schedule coaches across one-on-one coaching, live sessions, and fitness classes. Conduct regular team meetings and individual check-ins with coordinators and coaches. Manage workloads, coverage, and areas of specialty across multiple regions and time zones. Establish and uphold delivery standards for how events, outreach, and results are scheduled, tracked, and reported across all regions. Oversee the execution of campaigns, webinars, events, employee communications, coaching, and community activities. Translate program roadmaps into regional delivery plans, operational priorities, and measurable goals. Develop and maintain templates, checklists, playbooks, and operating procedures used by coordinators to prepare and run scheduled activities. Track team availability, coaching utilization, and upcoming delivery commitments to support capacity planning. Record delivered activities against contracted commitments and provide operational data for client reviews. Monitor regional performance across activity types, determine regional programming mix within the roadmap, and recommend roadmap adjustments when appropriate. Maintain operational trackers and coordinate access to internal and client systems with IT and Security teams. Manage day-to-day relationships and budgets for coaching vendors and contractors in partnership with People and Legal teams, ensuring work remains within contracted scope. Monitor service quality, participant feedback, and operational metrics, collaborating with internal leadership to resolve recurring issues and enhance delivery workflows. Exercise decision rights over coach and coordinator assignments, scheduling, regional programming mix, and delivery process changes, while escalating scope, budget, or headcount changes to the Account Director. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university. 5+ years of experience in program or service delivery operations. 3+ years of direct people management experience. Ability to consistently work hours that overlap with EMEA and APAC teams. Proven experience leading and developing a distributed team across multiple regions and time zones. Demonstrated experience overseeing ongoing client programs involving multiple activities, stakeholders, and delivery commitments. Experience coordinating contractors or specialized service providers while managing team coverage and capacity. Demonstrated ability to develop clear delivery processes, quality standards, and escalation paths. Experience using service data and participant feedback to resolve operational challenges and improve delivery performance. Compensation and Benefits Expected base salary range: $130,000 - $160,000 per year, dependent on factors such as experience and expertise. Eligibility for performance bonus and equity. Comprehensive health coverage, including medical, dental, and vision insurance. 401(k) retirement plan with organization match. Paid time off. Equal Opportunity Employer The organization is committed to creating a safe and welcoming work environment free of discrimination and harassment. Equal employment opportunity is provided to all employees and applicants regardless of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, genetics, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, family or parental status, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law. Reasonable accommodations are available for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans throughout the application and employment process.

review_candidates.title: Medical Monitor, South Korea
review_candidates.description: Who We Are Emerald Clinical Trials is a global leader in clinical research, partnering with over 160 biotech companies and 15 of the world’s top 20 pharmaceutical firms. Headquartered in Singapore, we combine scientific excellence with operational expertise to deliver end-to-end clinical trial solutions across all phases, offering Phase I-IV and real-world studies . With over 25 years of experience and a world-renowned focus in renal research , Emerald Clinical has helped drive medical breakthroughs through deep scientific insight, flawless execution, and an unwavering commitment to quality. Global Expertise. Local Insight. Real Impact. Emerald Clinical is where science, speed, and strategy come together to transform healthcare. For over 25 years, we have led the way in clinical research, combining global reach with deep Asia-Pacific expertise and unparalleled local insight to deliver smarter trials and stronger outcomes. Our 1000+ employees that span across Asia-Pacific, Europe, and the Americas are embedded in communities worldwide. We drive faster recruitment, deeper patient engagement, and meaningful results that move medicine forward. About The Role Provide medical oversight and support for clinical trials, ensuring studies are conducted safely, compliantly and scientifically per GCP and the protocol. Serve as the medical/clinical expert within the project team for study design, conduct, data interpretation and safety evaluation Responsibilities The key accountabilities listed below may not apply to every project that the Medical Monitor is assigned to support. Provide medical and academic expertise for new and existing Emerald Clinical studies Support Endpoint Adjudication and other relevant Committees where required Provide medical input to safety, endpoints documents and project plans as required Represent Emerald Clinical and its values with academic colleagues, commercial customers, vendors, government and regulatory bodies as requested Ensure activities comply with relevant Acts, legal demands and ethical standards Project development, initiation and support Provide clinical input into the development and/or review of study protocols, procedure manuals, data collection tools and data quality plans; Review query reports generated from project databases to identify errors and inconsistencies, as outlined in the medical monitoring plan. Provide ongoing, continuous support to sites by answering queries related to medical issues around patient eligibility, recruitment, treatment and management and adverse events etc. as outlined in the scope of the medical monitoring plan. Develop and provide protocol training from a medical perspective for project investigators and CRAs for the assigned projects, as required Provide input into ongoing training and education materials for project investigators e.g. study newsletters Endpoint adjudication activities Liaise with project teams, data management, endpoint coordinators, investigators, site staff, sponsors and endpoint adjudicators as needed Provide clinical input into development of endpoint adjudication manuals, plans, charters, tracking tools and associated documentation Provide medical review and input to endpoint packages as required Safety activities Liaise with internal and external stakeholders as appropriate Provide clinical input to development of safety manuals, plans, charters, tracking tools and associated documentation. Where contracted, review and provide narratives for Serious Adverse Events reported on Emerald Clinical trials according to timelines in the project plans. Provide medical advice and guidance for Emerald Clinical Safety team In collaboration with line manager, contribute to the development and provision of therapeutic area training for Emerald Clinical staff on a regular basis. Review literature and participate in conducting research that relates to the direct activities or interests of Emerald Clinical. About You Tertiary qualifications in Medicine, Pharmacy or life sciences education background. Master’s degree or above is preferred. Minimum of 3+ years of experience of medical monitoring or medical manager Fluent verbal and written English. Mandarin speaking skill is highly regarded. Working knowledge of current ICH/GCP, ethical and regulatory requirements Excellent attention to detail and accuracy Highly developed interpersonal, relationship building and negotiation skills Ability to work both independently and in a team environment Ability to perform multiple tasks and prioritise work effectively Why Join Us? At our core, Emerald Clinical Trials is committed to transforming clinical research by putting people first—both patients and our employees. By joining our team, you’ll be part of a global network of passionate professionals working together to deliver better research and outcomes for millions worldwide. Here’s What Makes Us Stand Out Purpose-Driven Work: You’ll contribute to clinical trials that genuinely improve lives, with a focus on therapies in renal, cardiometabolic, and oncology. Global Reach, Local Expertise: Our teams connect with local communities, building trust and meaningful engagement for every trial. Collaboration and Innovation: Work in a culture that values diverse perspectives and creative solutions to solve global health challenges. What We Offer We understand that great work happens when people feel valued and supported. That’s why we provide: Competitive Compensation: A tailored salary and benefits package to reflect your skills and experience. Flexibility: Enjoy hybrid or remote working arrangements, depending on your location and role. Career Growth: Access to a wealth of learning opportunities and a global network of scientific leaders to help you grow and develop in your role. Employee Wellbeing: Participate in programs and initiatives designed to promote work-life balance, health, and team connection, including global engagement surveys, recognition programs, and team-building events. Global Opportunities: Be part of a company with international reach, offering you exposure to diverse projects and clients. Interested? Apply now and help us achieve our mission to improve the health of millions worldwide. We are an equal-opportunity employer and encourage applications from all qualified candidates.

The specialist will conduct product presentations and remote demos, coordinate closely with the technical and marketing teams, and follow up on campaigns to convert prospects into opportunities. Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written, with the ability to engage professionally with clients across the GCC region. Familiarity with industrial or technology solutions, preferably in IoT, manufacturing, or predictive maintenance, is highly beneficial. Proficiency in CRM tools, basic sales analytics, and MS Office applications to manage leads, documentation, and reporting. Bachelor’s degree in Business, Engineering, or a related field; prior experience in inside sales or business development for international markets is an advantage. Ability to work on-site in Mumbai, collaborate with cross-functional teams, and adapt to a fast-paced, target-driven environment.
